---
title: "The Case for U-7: a ladder of labor underutilization from public CPS microdata"
author: "Mark G. Sheppard"
output: html_document
params:
  rebuild: false     # TRUE re-reads the IPUMS extract and rewrites data-source/u7/ (slow: two passes over ~80 million records)
  ddi: "~/Desktop/The Inequality of Recession/data/master/cps_00014.xml"   # IPUMS CPS Basic Monthly, 1976-2026, all persons
  alpha: 0.5         # recession threshold, percentage points
  k: 6               # smoothing window (months), as in the papers
  w: 12              # comparison window, current month included
  theta: 1           # skills mismatch: degree levels above the occupation's 75th percentile
  window: 5          # years in the rolling reference window for occupational requirements
---

This file builds the measures behind the three unlinked pages on the site, **The Case for U-7** (`#u7`), **Building U-7 from Public Data** (`#u7-data`) and **Who Counts in the Labor Force?** (`#u7-lfp`). It extends the Bureau of Labor Statistics' six measures of labor underutilization with four broader ones and runs every measure through the same turning-point rule as the rest of the site. The ladder runs from the narrowest measure to the broadest, jobless people before people with jobs: from U-3 up, each rung counts everyone the rung below it counts plus one more group, and a person who fits two groups is counted once, in the lower rung.

| Measure | Counts | Formula | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| U-1 | Unemployed 15 weeks or longer | U15 / LF | BLS (U1RATE) |
| U-2 | Job losers and people who completed temporary jobs | UL / LF | BLS (U2RATE) |
| U-3 | The unemployed | U / LF | BLS (UNRATE) |
| U-4 | + discouraged workers | (U + D) / (LF + D) | BLS (U4RATE) |
| U-5 | + other marginally attached | (U + MA) / (LF + MA) | BLS (U5RATE) |
| U-6 | + part time for economic reasons | (U + MA + PTER) / (LF + MA) | BLS (U6RATE) |
| **U-7** | **+ everyone else outside the labor force who wants a job** | (U + WJ + PTER) / (LF + WJ) | U-6 plus CPS microdata |
| U-8 | + own-account (unincorporated) self-employed | adds SEu to the U-7 numerator | U-6 plus CPS microdata |
| U-9 | + incorporated self-employed | adds SEi to the U-8 numerator | U-6 plus CPS microdata |
| U-10 | + skills-mismatched workers | adds SM to the U-9 numerator | U-6 plus CPS microdata |

U-1 and U-2 are slices of U-3 rather than rungs: they overlap, and U-1 has at times been above U-2, as in several months between 2011 and 2014. WJ is everyone outside the labor force who says they want a job (`WNLOOK`), which includes the marginally attached. U-8 and U-9 follow `gig_work_rates_U7_U10.Rmd`: own-account and incorporated self-employment (`CLASSWKR` 13 and 14) as the margins of independent and gig work, counting the self-employed not part time for economic reasons. Multiple jobholding, the other gig margin in that file, needs the IPUMS variable `MULTJOB`, which this extract does not include; it is meant to replace incorporated self-employment as U-9 once an extract has it. U-10 adds the measure in the RDC proposal, skills mismatch, at the top of the ladder. A worker is **skills-mismatched** (SM) when their highest degree is at least `theta` degree levels above the 75th percentile of degrees held by workers in the same occupation (a realized-matches definition). Degree levels: no high-school diploma, high-school diploma (including some college without a degree), associate, bachelor's, master's, professional or doctorate. Occupational requirements come from a rolling reference window, the previous `window` years of CPS data, phased in month by month so that no January jumps appear; workers already counted as part time for economic reasons or as self-employed are not counted again.

**Data.** U-3 to U-6 are the official seasonally adjusted BLS series (FRED, in `data-source/tool-data`). Everything beyond U-6 comes from the IPUMS CPS Basic Monthly files (`cps_00014`, January 1994 to September 2026, civilians 16 and older, final weights `WTFINL`), aggregated into the files in `data-source/u7/`:

* `u7_groups.csv`: monthly weighted counts by race and ethnicity (labor force, employed, unemployed, part time for economic reasons, not in the labor force but wanting a job, self-employed, and so on);
* `u7_cells.csv.gz`: employed workers by month, occupation (`OCC2010`), degree level and class (part time for economic reasons, own-account self-employed, incorporated self-employed, other), 1994 on;
* `u7_groupcells.csv.gz`: labor force, unemployment, part-time and skills-mismatch counts by month, race, sex, age, nativity and education, with mismatch measured with the main definition;
* `u7_crosswalk.csv`: monthly mismatch counts under the major-group requirement crosswalk in `The Case for U7.Rmd`, for comparison;
* `occ2010_labels.csv`: the IPUMS titles of the `OCC2010` codes;
* `u7_agesex.csv`, `u7_prime.csv`, `u7_flows.csv`: for the participation page (`#u7-lfp`), population, labor force and employment by month, age group, sex and nativity; the pieces of every measure for ages 25 to 54, with reasons for being out of the labor force; and prime-age flows between labor-force states from one month to the next.

These tabulations were first produced by a streaming reader run over the raw `cps_00014.dat.gz` on the Mac, which implements the same rules as the `rebuild-pass1`, `rebuild-pass2` and `rebuild-pass3` chunks below; on a 500,000-record test sample from 2016 to 2022 the two give identical counts, including the month-to-month flows. Set `rebuild: true` to recreate them in R from the extract.

U-7 to U-10 take the unemployed and the part time for economic reasons from the official series and the rest from the microdata. With $u_3 = U/LF$, $m = MA/LF$ and $p = PTER/LF$, the official $U5 = (u_3 + m)/(1 + m)$ gives $m = (U5 - U3)/(1 - U5)$, and $U6 = (u_3 + m + p)/(1 + m)$ gives $p$; then $U7 = (u_3 + wj + p)/(1 + wj)$ with $wj = WJ/LF$ from the microdata. The marginally attached themselves cannot be identified in this extract (it has the reason for not looking, `WNLOOK`, but not availability or past-year search), so $m$ is used only to split U-10 into its parts and for the prime-age measures. October 2025, when the federal shutdown cancelled the household survey, is interpolated, as everywhere on the site.

**Turning points.** Every series is scored with the site's rule (the `k`-month average minus its minimum over the last `w` months, threshold `alpha`), matched to the 2001, 2007-09 and 2020 recessions between 18 months before and 12 months after each NBER peak, with thresholds also scaled to each measure's level or volatility as in the site's "Threshold scaling" control. Precision is the share of all crossings since 1995 that fall inside those windows. The JavaScript on the pages recomputes the same numbers from `data/u7_series.csv`, so the series are rounded to six decimals before they are scored here.

**Participation.** The `participation` chunk measures prime-age (25-54) participation, employment, reasons for being out of the labor force and month-to-month flows, counts the prime-age adults missing relative to 2000, 2007 and 2019 participation rates by age and sex, and recomputes U-1 to U-10 under six assumptions about who is in the labor force: as measured; everyone who wants a job; prime-age participation at 2019 or at 2000 rates; prime-age adults only; and every prime-age adult.

**Outputs.** `data/u7_series.csv` (every measure, its components and the subgroup series, seasonally adjusted), `data/u7_summary.json` (the numbers quoted on the U-7 pages), and `data/u7_lfp.csv` and `data/u7_lfp.json` for the participation page.

```{r setup}
suppressMessages({ library(data.table); library(zoo); library(forecast); library(jsonlite) })
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))   # repository root
```

```{r helpers}
mi  <- function(s) as.integer(substr(s, 1, 4)) * 12L + as.integer(substr(s, 6, 7)) - 1L
lab <- function(t) sprintf("%d-%02d", t %/% 12L, t %% 12L + 1L)
# Same seasonal adjustment as every other microdata series on the site (three-month centered average, then STL)
sa <- function(x) {
  x  <- zoo::na.approx(x, na.rm = FALSE, rule = 2)
  xs <- as.numeric(zoo::rollmean(zoo::zoo(x), k = 3, fill = NA, align = "center"))
  xs[is.na(xs)] <- x[is.na(xs)]
  as.numeric(forecast::seasadj(stl(ts(xs, frequency = 12), s.window = "periodic", robust = TRUE, t.window = 13)))
}
# The same adjustment without the three-month average, used only to compare with the official (unsmoothed) series
sa_raw <- function(x) {
  x <- zoo::na.approx(x, na.rm = FALSE, rule = 2)
  as.numeric(forecast::seasadj(stl(ts(x, frequency = 12), s.window = "periodic", robust = TRUE, t.window = 13)))
}
# Turning-point indicator: k-month average minus its minimum over the last w months (current month included)
rule <- function(x, k = params$k, w = params$w) {
  a <- frollmean(x, k, align = "right", algo = "exact")
  a - frollapply(a, w, min, align = "right")
}
NB <- data.table(id = c("2001", "2007", "2020"), peak = mi(c("2001-03", "2007-12", "2020-02")),
                 trough = mi(c("2001-11", "2009-06", "2020-04")), prev = mi(c("1991-03", "2001-11", "2009-06")))
# Episodes above the threshold, as in the site's JavaScript (missing months are skipped, not breaks)
episodes <- function(ind, alpha) {
  out <- list(); cur <- NULL; f <- which(!is.na(ind))[1]
  if (is.na(f)) return(out)
  for (i in f:length(ind)) {
    x <- ind[i]; if (is.na(x)) next
    if (is.null(cur) && x >= alpha) cur <- c(on = i, off = NA)
    else if (!is.null(cur) && x < alpha) { cur[["off"]] <- i; out[[length(out) + 1]] <- cur; cur <- NULL }
  }
  if (!is.null(cur)) out[[length(out) + 1]] <- cur
  out
}
# Match a series' signal to one recession: first episode starting between 18 months before and 12 months after the
# NBER peak (not before the previous trough); "continuing" if an episode is already under way when the window opens
match_rec <- function(ind, t, r, alpha, before = 18L, after = 12L) {
  R <- NB[id == r]; W0 <- max(R$peak - before, R$prev + 1L); W1 <- R$peak + after
  i0 <- match(W0, t); i1 <- match(W1, t); f <- which(!is.na(ind))[1]
  out <- list(status = "no data", on = NA_integer_, lead = NA_real_, exit = NA_integer_, dur = NA_real_, after_trough = NA_real_)
  if (is.na(i0) || is.na(f) || f > i0) return(out)
  eps <- episodes(ind, alpha)
  if (any(vapply(eps, function(e) e[["on"]] < i0 && (is.na(e[["off"]]) || e[["off"]] > i0), logical(1)))) { out$status <- "continuing"; return(out) }
  hit <- Filter(function(e) e[["on"]] >= i0 && e[["on"]] <= i1, eps)
  if (!length(hit)) { out$status <- "no signal"; return(out) }
  e <- hit[[1]]; on <- t[e[["on"]]]; ex <- if (is.na(e[["off"]])) NA_integer_ else t[e[["off"]]]
  list(status = "ok", on = on, lead = R$peak - on, exit = ex, dur = ex - on, after_trough = ex - R$trough)
}
starts_of <- function(ind, alpha) {
  on <- !is.na(ind) & ind >= alpha
  which(on & !c(FALSE, on[-length(on)]) & c(FALSE, !is.na(ind[-length(ind)])))
}
in_window <- function(s) vapply(s, function(x) any(x >= NB$peak - 18L & x <= NB$peak + 12L), logical(1))
# Threshold scaling, as the site's "Threshold scaling" control: by mean level, or by the volatility of 12-month changes
alpha_for <- function(x, base, scale, alpha = params$alpha, k = params$k) {
  if (scale == "fixed") return(alpha)
  ok <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(base)
  if (scale == "level") return(alpha * mean(x[ok]) / mean(base[ok]))
  a1 <- frollmean(x, k, algo = "exact"); a2 <- frollmean(base, k, algo = "exact")
  d1 <- a1 - shift(a1, 12); d2 <- a2 - shift(a2, 12); ok2 <- !is.na(d1) & !is.na(d2)
  alpha * sd(d1[ok2]) / sd(d2[ok2])
}
score <- function(x, t, base, scale = "fixed") {
  a <- alpha_for(x, base, scale); ind <- rule(x)
  m <- setNames(lapply(NB$id, function(r) match_rec(ind, t, r, a)), NB$id)
  s <- t[starts_of(ind, a)]
  list(alpha = a, m = m, sig = s, n_true = sum(in_window(s)), false = s[!in_window(s)], ind = ind)
}
```

```{r rebuild-pass1, eval = params$rebuild}
# Re-aggregate the IPUMS extract, pass 1: u7_groups.csv and u7_cells.csv.gz. Pass 2 (u7_groupcells.csv.gz and
# u7_crosswalk.csv) needs the occupational requirements, so it runs after the thresholds chunk.
library(ipumsr)
ddi <- read_ipums_ddi(path.expand(params$ddi))
vars <- c("YEAR", "MONTH", "WTFINL", "AGE", "SEX", "RACE", "HISPAN", "NATIVITY", "EMPSTAT", "LABFORCE", "OCC2010", "CLASSWKR",
          "DURUNEMP", "WHYUNEMP", "WNLOOK", "WKSTAT", "EDUC")
lev_of <- function(educ) fcase(educ >= 2L & educ <= 72L, 0L, educ %in% c(73L, 81L), 1L, educ %in% c(91L, 92L), 2L,
                               educ == 111L, 3L, educ == 123L, 4L, educ %in% c(124L, 125L), 5L, default = -1L)
prep <- function(x) {
  d <- as.data.table(lapply(x, function(col) { attributes(col) <- NULL; col })); setnames(d, tolower(names(d)))
  d <- d[age >= 16 & empstat >= 10]                       # civilians 16 and older
  d[, `:=`(date = sprintf("%d-%02d", as.integer(year), as.integer(month)), w = as.numeric(wtfinl),
           emp = empstat %in% c(10L, 12L), une = empstat %in% 20:22, nilf = labforce == 1L, lev = lev_of(as.integer(educ)))]
  d[, pter := emp & wkstat %in% 20:22]
  d[, wj := nilf & ((wnlook >= 1L & wnlook <= 11L) | wnlook == 997L)]
  d[, race5 := fifelse(hispan >= 100L & hispan < 900L, "Hispanic", fifelse(race == 100L, "White", fifelse(race == 200L, "Black",
               fifelse(race %in% c(650L, 651L, 652L), "Asian", "Other"))))]
  d[]
}
pass1 <- function(d) list(
  g = d[, .(pop = sum(w), lf = sum(w * (labforce == 2L)), emp = sum(w * emp), une = sum(w * une),
            u15 = sum(w * (une & durunemp >= 15L & durunemp < 999L)), ulos = sum(w * (une & whyunemp %in% 1:3)),
            pter = sum(w * pter), ptne = sum(w * (emp & wkstat %in% c(12L, 40L, 41L))), ftpe = sum(w * (emp & wkstat == 14L)),
            nilf = sum(w * nilf), wj = sum(w * wj), wjmk = sum(w * (nilf & wnlook >= 1L & wnlook <= 5L)),
            seu = sum(w * (emp & classwkr == 13L)), sei = sum(w * (emp & classwkr == 14L)), fam = sum(w * (emp & classwkr == 29L)),
            n_lf = sum(labforce == 2L), n_emp = sum(emp)), by = .(date, group = race5)],
  c = d[emp & year >= 1992 & occ2010 > 0 & occ2010 < 9800 & lev >= 0L,
        .(w = sum(w), n = .N), by = .(date, occ2010, lev, cls = fcase(pter, 1L, classwkr == 13L, 2L, classwkr == 14L, 3L, default = 0L))])
acc <- list()
read_ipums_micro_chunked(ddi, IpumsSideEffectCallback$new(function(x, pos) { acc[[length(acc) + 1]] <<- pass1(prep(x)) }),
                         chunk_size = 2e6, vars = vars, verbose = FALSE)
G1 <- rbindlist(lapply(acc, `[[`, "g"))[, lapply(.SD, sum), by = .(date, group)]
G1 <- rbind(G1[, lapply(.SD, sum), by = date, .SDcols = !"group"][, group := "All"], G1, use.names = TRUE)
fwrite(G1[order(group, date)], "data-source/u7/u7_groups.csv")
fwrite(rbindlist(lapply(acc, `[[`, "c"))[, .(w = sum(w), n = sum(n)), by = .(date, occ2010, lev, cls)][order(date, occ2010, lev, cls)],
       "data-source/u7/u7_cells.csv.gz")
rm(acc); gc()
```

```{r thresholds}
CL <- fread("data-source/u7/u7_cells.csv.gz")[date >= "1994-01"]
CL[, `:=`(yr = as.integer(substr(date, 1, 4)), mo = as.integer(substr(date, 6, 7)))]
# 75th percentile of degree level among the workers in each occupation, pooled over the months in d
p75 <- function(d) {
  d <- d[, .(w = sum(w)), by = .(occ2010, lev)][order(occ2010, lev)]
  d[, cs := cumsum(w) / sum(w), by = occ2010]
  d[cs >= 0.75 - 1e-12, .(p75 = min(lev)), by = occ2010]
}
# Requirements used in year y: the previous L years (the first L years of data, for the earliest years)
ref_years <- function(y, L) {
  lo <- max(1994L, y - L); hi <- y - 1L
  if (hi < 1994L + L - 1L) { lo <- 1994L; hi <- 1994L + L - 1L }
  c(lo, hi)
}
thr_table <- function(L) rbindlist(lapply(1993:2026, function(y) { r <- ref_years(y, L); cbind(year = y, p75(CL[yr >= r[1] & yr <= r[2]])) }))
POOLED <- p75(CL)            # one set of requirements for the whole period: the fallback, and the "fixed" variant
TH <- thr_table(params$window)
table(POOLED$p75)            # occupations by required degree level (0 none ... 5 professional or doctorate)
```

```{r rebuild-pass2, eval = params$rebuild}
# Pass 2: subgroup cells with the main mismatch definition, and the crosswalk comparison
xw <- data.table(lo = c(10, 500, 1000, 1300, 1600, 2000, 2100, 2200, 2600, 3000, 3600, 3700, 4000, 4200, 4300, 4700, 5000, 6000, 6200, 7000, 7700, 9000),
                 hi = c(430, 950, 1240, 1560, 1980, 2060, 2160, 2550, 2960, 3540, 3655, 3955, 4160, 4250, 4650, 4965, 5940, 6130, 6940, 7630, 8965, 9750),
                 req = c(111, 111, 111, 111, 111, 111, 123, 111, 80, 111, 73, 73, 60, 60, 73, 73, 73, 60, 73, 73, 73, 60))
req_of <- integer(10000); for (i in seq_len(nrow(xw))) req_of[(xw$lo[i]:xw$hi[i]) + 1L] <- as.integer(xw$req[i])
pass2 <- function(d) {
  d <- d[year >= 1994]
  d[, `:=`(yr = as.integer(year), mo = as.integer(month))]
  d <- merge(d, TH[, .(yr = year + 1L, occ2010, p0 = p75)], by = c("yr", "occ2010"), all.x = TRUE)
  d <- merge(d, TH[, .(yr = year, occ2010, p1 = p75)], by = c("yr", "occ2010"), all.x = TRUE)
  d <- merge(d, POOLED[, .(occ2010, pA = p75)], by = "occ2010", all.x = TRUE)
  d[is.na(p0), p0 := pA]; d[is.na(p1), p1 := pA]
  d[, ok := emp & occ2010 > 0 & occ2010 < 9800 & lev >= 0L & !is.na(pA)]
  d[, smf := fifelse(ok, (1 - mo / 12) * (lev >= p0 + params$theta) + (mo / 12) * (lev >= p1 + params$theta), 0)]
  d[, smA := fifelse(ok, as.numeric(lev >= pA + params$theta), 0)]
  d[, `:=`(sx = fifelse(sex == 2L, "F", "M"), fb = as.integer(nativity == 5L),
           ag = fcase(age < 22L, "16-21", age < 28L, "22-27", age < 35L, "28-34", age < 55L, "35-54", default = "55+"),
           e4 = fcase(lev <= 0L, "LTHS", lev == 1L, "HS", lev == 2L, "Assoc", default = "BAplus"))]
  d[, el := fcase(educ <= 1L | educ == 999L, 0L, educ < 73L, 60L, educ == 73L, 73L, educ >= 80L & educ < 111L, 80L,
                  educ == 111L, 111L, educ >= 123L, 123L, default = 0L)]
  d[, rq := req_of[pmin(pmax(occ2010, 0L), 9999L) + 1L]]
  d[, over := emp & rq > 0L & el > 0L & el > rq]
  list(gc = d[, .(lf = sum(w * (labforce == 2L)), emp = sum(w * emp), une = sum(w * une), pter = sum(w * pter), wj = sum(w * wj),
                  smP = sum(w * smf * !pter), smP_all = sum(w * smf), smA = sum(w * smA * !pter),
                  seu = sum(w * (1 - smf) * (emp & !pter & classwkr == 13L)), sei = sum(w * (1 - smf) * (emp & !pter & classwkr == 14L)),
                  n_emp = sum(emp), n_lf = sum(labforce == 2L)), by = .(date, race = race5, sex = sx, age = ag, fborn = fb, educ = e4)],
       cw = d[, .(cw_all = sum(w * over), cw_np = sum(w * (over & !pter))), by = date])
}
acc <- list()
read_ipums_micro_chunked(ddi, IpumsSideEffectCallback$new(function(x, pos) { acc[[length(acc) + 1]] <<- pass2(prep(x)) }),
                         chunk_size = 2e6, vars = vars, verbose = FALSE)
gcols <- c("date", "race", "sex", "age", "fborn", "educ")
fwrite(rbindlist(lapply(acc, `[[`, "gc"))[, lapply(.SD, sum), by = gcols][lf + emp + wj > 0][order(date, race, sex, age, fborn, educ)], "data-source/u7/u7_groupcells.csv.gz")
fwrite(rbindlist(lapply(acc, `[[`, "cw"))[, lapply(.SD, sum), by = date][order(date)], "data-source/u7/u7_crosswalk.csv")
rm(acc); gc()
```

```{r rebuild-pass3, eval = params$rebuild}
# Pass 3: participation diagnostics. Age x sex x nativity cells (16+); prime-age (25-54) pieces by sex and nativity;
# prime-age flows between consecutive months, linking people with CPSIDP (same sex, age the same or one year older,
# rotation group one higher), weighted with the earlier month's final weight
vars3 <- c(vars, "MISH", "CPSIDP", "ASECFLAG")
AGEB <- c(16, 20, 25, 35, 45, 55, 60, 65, 70); AGEL <- c("16-19", "20-24", "25-34", "35-44", "45-54", "55-59", "60-64", "65-69", "70+")
pass3 <- function(d) {
  d <- d[year >= 1994 & (is.na(asecflag) | asecflag != 1L)]   # ASECFLAG is blank outside March
  d[, ri := .I]
  d[, `:=`(yr = as.integer(year), mo = as.integer(month), sx = fifelse(sex == 2L, "F", "M"), fb = as.integer(nativity == 5L), ab = AGEL[findInterval(age, AGEB)])]
  d <- merge(d, TH[, .(yr = year + 1L, occ2010, p0 = p75)], by = c("yr", "occ2010"), all.x = TRUE)
  d <- merge(d, TH[, .(yr = year, occ2010, p1 = p75)], by = c("yr", "occ2010"), all.x = TRUE)
  d <- merge(d, POOLED[, .(occ2010, pA = p75)], by = "occ2010", all.x = TRUE)
  setorder(d, ri)
  d[is.na(p0), p0 := pA]; d[is.na(p1), p1 := pA]
  d[, smf := fifelse(emp & occ2010 > 0 & occ2010 < 9800 & lev >= 0L & !is.na(pA), (1 - mo / 12) * (lev >= p0 + params$theta) + (mo / 12) * (lev >= p1 + params$theta), 0)]
  p <- d[age >= 25 & age <= 54]
  list(cells = d[, .(pop = sum(w), lf = sum(w * (labforce == 2L)), emp = sum(w * emp)), by = .(date, age = ab, sex = sx, fborn = fb)],
       pr = p[, .(pop = sum(w), lf = sum(w * (labforce == 2L)), emp = sum(w * emp), une = sum(w * une),
                  u15 = sum(w * (une & durunemp >= 15L & durunemp < 999L)), ulos = sum(w * (une & whyunemp %in% 1:3)), pter = sum(w * pter),
                  nilf = sum(w * nilf), wj = sum(w * wj), wjmk = sum(w * (nilf & wnlook >= 1L & wnlook <= 5L)), n_want = sum(w * wj),
                  n_disab = sum(w * (nilf & !wj & empstat == 32L)), n_school = sum(w * (nilf & !wj & empstat == 33L)),
                  n_retired = sum(w * (nilf & !wj & empstat == 36L)), n_other = sum(w * (nilf & !wj & !empstat %in% c(32L, 33L, 36L))),
                  w_mkt = sum(w * (wj & wnlook >= 1L & wnlook <= 5L)), w_family = sum(w * (wj & wnlook %in% 6:7)), w_school = sum(w * (wj & wnlook == 8L)),
                  w_health = sum(w * (wj & wnlook == 9L)), w_other = sum(w * (wj & wnlook %in% c(10L, 11L, 997L))),
                  smP = sum(w * smf * !pter), seu = sum(w * (1 - smf) * (emp & !pter & classwkr == 13L)),
                  sei = sum(w * (1 - smf) * (emp & !pter & classwkr == 14L)), n_pop = .N, n_lf = sum(labforce == 2L)), by = .(date, sex = sx, fborn = fb)],
       link = d[cpsidp > 0, .(ym = yr * 12L + mo - 1L, date, pid = cpsidp, mish, age, sex = sx, st = fcase(emp, "E", une, "U", default = "N"), w)])
}
flows_add <- function(prev, cur) {
  if (is.null(prev) || cur$ym[1] != prev$ym[1] + 1L) return(NULL)
  j <- merge(unique(prev, by = "pid")[, .(pid, mish0 = mish, age0 = age, sex0 = sex, st0 = st, w0 = w)],
             unique(cur, by = "pid")[, .(pid, date, mish, age, sex, st)], by = "pid")
  j[sex0 == sex & age - age0 >= 0 & age - age0 <= 1 & mish == mish0 + 1L & age0 >= 25 & age0 <= 54, .(w = sum(w0)), by = .(date, sex = sex0, from = st0, to = st)]
}
acc3 <- list(); fl3 <- list(); prev <- NULL; pend <- NULL
step <- function(link) {                       # months can straddle chunks: finish every month but the last one seen
  Lk <- rbind(pend, link); ms <- sort(unique(Lk$ym))
  for (m in head(ms, -1)) { cur <- Lk[ym == m]; fl3[[length(fl3) + 1]] <<- flows_add(prev, cur); prev <<- cur }
  pend <<- Lk[ym == tail(ms, 1)]
}
read_ipums_micro_chunked(ddi, IpumsSideEffectCallback$new(function(x, pos) { r <- pass3(prep(x)); acc3[[length(acc3) + 1]] <<- r[c("cells", "pr")]; if (nrow(r$link)) step(r$link) }),
                         chunk_size = 2e6, vars = vars3, verbose = FALSE)
fl3[[length(fl3) + 1]] <- flows_add(prev, pend)
fwrite(rbindlist(lapply(acc3, `[[`, "cells"))[, lapply(.SD, sum), by = .(date, age, sex, fborn)][order(date, age, sex, fborn)], "data-source/u7/u7_agesex.csv")
fwrite(rbindlist(lapply(acc3, `[[`, "pr"))[, lapply(.SD, sum), by = .(date, sex, fborn)][order(date, sex, fborn)], "data-source/u7/u7_prime.csv")
fwrite(rbindlist(fl3)[, .(w = sum(w)), by = .(date, sex, from, to)][order(date, sex, from, to)], "data-source/u7/u7_flows.csv")
rm(acc3, fl3, prev, pend); gc()
```

```{r mismatch}
# Monthly counts for the rungs above U-7 under a set of mismatch requirements (NULL = pooled, fixed), phased in month by month.
# Counting order follows the ladder: se and sei are the own-account and incorporated self-employed not part time for economic
# reasons (U-8 and U-9), whatever their degree; sm is the skills-mismatched not already counted (U-10): not part time for
# economic reasons and not self-employed. sm_np is every mismatched worker not part time for economic reasons, and sm_seu and
# sm_sei the mismatched among the self-employed, for the checks and the prime-age split below.
sm_counts <- function(TH = NULL, theta = params$theta) {
  x <- merge(CL, POOLED[, .(occ2010, pA = p75)], by = "occ2010")
  if (is.null(TH)) x[, f := as.numeric(lev >= pA + theta)] else {
    x <- merge(x, TH[, .(yr = year + 1L, occ2010, p0 = p75)], by = c("yr", "occ2010"), all.x = TRUE)
    x <- merge(x, TH[, .(yr = year, occ2010, p1 = p75)], by = c("yr", "occ2010"), all.x = TRUE)
    x[is.na(p0), p0 := pA]; x[is.na(p1), p1 := pA]
    x[, f := (1 - mo / 12) * (lev >= p0 + theta) + (mo / 12) * (lev >= p1 + theta)]
  }
  x <- x[, .(sm = sum(w * f * (cls == 0L)), sm_np = sum(w * f * (cls != 1L)), sm_all = sum(w * f), sm_seu = sum(w * f * (cls == 2L)),
             sm_sei = sum(w * f * (cls == 3L)), se = sum(w * (cls == 2L)), sei = sum(w * (cls == 3L))), by = date]
  x[D[, .(date)], on = "date"]
}
# January 2003: the CPS moved to the 2000 Census occupation codes, which shifts every occupation-based count.
# The level before the break is moved by the January jump net of the usual January change (three-month means each side).
brk <- function(x, at = "2003-01") {
  i <- match(at, D$date)
  jump <- function(j) mean(x[j:(j + 2)], na.rm = TRUE) - mean(x[(j - 3):(j - 1)], na.rm = TRUE)
  jan <- setdiff(which(substr(D$date, 6, 7) == "01" & seq_len(nrow(D)) > 3 & seq_len(nrow(D)) <= nrow(D) - 2), i)
  d <- jump(i) - mean(vapply(jan, jump, 0))
  x[seq_len(i - 1)] <- x[seq_len(i - 1)] + d
  attr(x, "break") <- d
  x
}
V <- list(main = sm_counts(TH), w3 = sm_counts(thr_table(3)), w10 = sm_counts(thr_table(10)), fixed = sm_counts(NULL),
          theta2 = sm_counts(TH, theta = 2))
# The crosswalk counts carry no class of worker, so the self-employed among them are removed in the main definition's
# proportion; the self-employment rungs do not depend on the mismatch definition
V$crosswalk <- CW[D[, .(date)], on = "date"][, .(date, sm = cw_np * V$main$sm / V$main$sm_np, sm_all = cw_all, se = V$main$se, sei = V$main$sei)]
# check: the subgroup cells were built with the same main definition
chk <- merge(V$main[, .(date, sm_np)], GC[, .(smP = sum(smP)), by = date], by = "date")
stopifnot(max(abs(chk$sm_np / chk$smP - 1)) < 1e-4)
comp <- lapply(V, function(v) {
  r <- list(sm = brk(v$sm / D$lf), se = brk(v$se / D$lf), sei = brk(v$sei / D$lf))
  list(sm = sa(r$sm), se = sa(r$se), sei = sa(r$sei), break_sm = attr(r$sm, "break"))
})
sapply(comp, function(z) round(100 * z$break_sm, 2))   # size of the 2003 coding break, percentage points of the labor force
```

```{r ladder}
L <- D[, .(date, t, U1 = U1RATE, U2 = U2RATE, U3 = UNRATE, U4 = U4RATE, U5 = U5RATE, U6 = U6RATE)]
L[, m := (U5 - U3) / (100 - U5)]               # marginally attached per labor-force member, from the official U-5
L[, p := (U6 - U5) / 100 * (1 + m)]            # part time for economic reasons per labor-force member, from the official U-6
L[, wj := sa(D$wj / D$lf)]                     # everyone not in the labor force who wants a job (includes the marginally attached)
stopifnot(all(L$wj > L$m))                     # the want-a-job pool contains the marginally attached, so U-7 is never below U-6
# From U-7 up the denominator is LF + WJ, and each rung adds one group to the numerator: the rest of the want-a-job pool (U-7),
# the own-account self-employed (U-8), the incorporated self-employed (U-9), and skills-mismatched workers not already counted (U-10)
rungs <- function(c) {
  b <- L$U3 / 100 + L$wj + L$p
  list(U7 = 100 * b / (1 + L$wj), U8 = 100 * (b + c$se) / (1 + L$wj), U9 = 100 * (b + c$se + c$sei) / (1 + L$wj),
       U10 = 100 * (b + c$se + c$sei + c$sm) / (1 + L$wj))
}
R <- rungs(comp$main)
for (nm in names(R)) L[, (nm) := R[[nm]]]
for (v in c("w3", "w10", "fixed", "theta2", "crosswalk")) L[, (paste0("U10_", v)) := rungs(comp[[v]])$U10]
# U-10 split into its parts, all over U-10's denominator, so they add up to U-10
L[, `:=`(c_u = U3 / (1 + wj), c_ma = 100 * m / (1 + wj), c_pt = 100 * p / (1 + wj), c_wj = 100 * (wj - m) / (1 + wj),
         c_seu = 100 * comp$main$se / (1 + wj), c_sei = 100 * comp$main$sei / (1 + wj), c_sm = 100 * comp$main$sm / (1 + wj))]
stopifnot(max(abs(L[, c_u + c_ma + c_pt + c_wj + c_seu + c_sei + c_sm] - L$U10)) < 1e-9,
          all(L$U7 >= L$U6), all(L$U8 >= L$U7), all(L$U9 >= L$U8), all(L$U10 >= L$U9))
# Every series is rounded to six decimals here, as written to data/u7_series.csv, so the site's JavaScript and this file
# score exactly the same numbers (a value that rounds to the threshold could otherwise fall on different sides of it)
LADDER <- paste0("U", 1:10)
SER <- c(LADDER, paste0("U10_", c("w3", "w10", "fixed", "theta2", "crosswalk")), "c_u", "c_ma", "c_pt", "c_wj", "c_seu", "c_sei", "c_sm")
L[, (SER) := lapply(.SD, round, 6), .SDcols = SER]
L[date == max(date), c(list(date = date), lapply(.SD, round, 1)), .SDcols = LADDER]
L[, lapply(.SD, function(x) round(mean(x), 1)), .SDcols = LADDER]
```

```{r turning-points}
tp_table <- function(S, names, scale) rbindlist(lapply(names, function(nm) {
  s <- score(S[[nm]], L$t, L$U3, scale)
  data.table(measure = nm, scale = scale, alpha = s$alpha, rec = NB$id,
             status = vapply(s$m, function(z) z$status, ""), onset = vapply(s$m, function(z) if (is.na(z$on)) NA_character_ else lab(z$on), ""),
             lead = vapply(s$m, function(z) z$lead, 0), dur = vapply(s$m, function(z) z$dur, 0),
             after_trough = vapply(s$m, function(z) z$after_trough, 0),
             n_sig = length(s$sig), n_true = s$n_true, false = paste(lab(s$false), collapse = " "))
}))
TP <- rbindlist(lapply(c("fixed", "level", "vol"), function(sc) tp_table(L, LADDER, sc)))
TP <- merge(TP, TP[measure == "U3", .(scale, rec, lead_u3 = lead)], by = c("scale", "rec"))
TP[, head_start := lead - lead_u3]
dcast(TP[scale == "fixed"], measure ~ rec, value.var = "lead")
TP[scale == "fixed" & rec == "2001", .(measure, alpha, n_sig, n_true, precision = round(100 * n_true / n_sig), false)]
dcast(TP, measure + scale ~ rec, value.var = "lead")
# Robustness: the classic Sahm rule (three-month average against the minimum of the previous 12 months)
classic <- rbindlist(lapply(LADDER, function(nm) {
  a <- frollmean(L[[nm]], 3); ind <- a - shift(frollapply(a, 12, min), 1)
  m <- lapply(NB$id, function(r) match_rec(ind, L$t, r, params$alpha)); s <- L$t[starts_of(ind, params$alpha)]
  data.table(measure = nm, rec = NB$id, lead = vapply(m, function(z) z$lead, 0), n_sig = length(s), n_true = sum(in_window(s)))
}))
dcast(classic, measure + n_sig + n_true ~ rec, value.var = "lead")
```

```{r cycle}
# The rungs over the cycle. Does each added group move with U-6, or against it? The want-a-job pool is jobless, like the
# groups in U-4 to U-6; the self-employed and the mismatched are slices of employment.
ch12 <- function(x) { a <- frollmean(x, params$k); a - shift(a, 12) }
L[, c_se := c_seu + c_sei]                     # both self-employment rungs, in U-10 points
cor6 <- function(x) cor(ch12(x), ch12(L$U6), use = "complete.obs")
cyc <- list(cor_wj_u6 = cor6(L$c_wj), cor_se_u6 = cor6(L$c_se), cor_sm_u6 = cor6(L$c_sm),
            sd12 = sapply(L[, c(LADDER, "c_wj", "c_se", "c_sm"), with = FALSE], function(x) sd(ch12(x), na.rm = TRUE)))
# change in U-6 and in the parts above it from the peak to a year after the trough, and over the next three years
at <- function(x, tt) x[match(tt, L$t)]
cyc$recessions <- NB[, .(id, u6_down = at(L$U6, trough + 12L) - at(L$U6, peak), wj_down = at(L$c_wj, trough + 12L) - at(L$c_wj, peak),
                         se_down = at(L$c_se, trough + 12L) - at(L$c_se, peak), sm_down = at(L$c_sm, trough + 12L) - at(L$c_sm, peak),
                         u6_up = at(L$U6, trough + 48L) - at(L$U6, trough + 12L), sm_up = at(L$c_sm, trough + 48L) - at(L$c_sm, trough + 12L))]
# Recovery: share of each measure's recession rise (pre-recession low to recession high, six-month averages) still left 2 and 4 years after the trough
recov <- rbindlist(lapply(LADDER, function(nm) {
  a <- frollmean(L[[nm]], params$k)
  NB[, { lo <- min(at(a, (peak - 12L):peak)); hi <- max(at(a, peak:(trough + 24L)))
         .(measure = nm, low = lo, high = hi, left24 = (at(a, trough + 24L) - lo) / (hi - lo), left48 = (at(a, trough + 48L) - lo) / (hi - lo)) }, by = id]
}))
cyc[c("cor_wj_u6", "cor_se_u6", "cor_sm_u6")]; cyc$recessions; recov
```

```{r participation}
lf_sa <- sa(D$lf)

# Prime-age flows: the share of each month's employed (E), unemployed (U) and non-participants (N) found in each state the next month
FW <- dcast(FL[, .(w = sum(w)), by = .(date, from, to)], date ~ from + to, value.var = "w", fill = 0)[D[, .(date)], on = "date"]
# months the CPS links only partly (household identifiers changed in mid-1995) are treated as missing and interpolated
FW[, tot := E_E + E_U + E_N + U_E + U_U + U_N + N_E + N_U + N_N]
FW[is.na(tot) | tot < 0.5 * median(tot, na.rm = TRUE), setdiff(names(FW), "date") := NA]
fr <- function(a, b) { o <- FW[[paste0(a, "_", b)]] / (FW[[paste0(a, "_E")]] + FW[[paste0(a, "_U")]] + FW[[paste0(a, "_N")]]); round(100 * sa(o), 6) }
LFP[, `:=`(f_EN = fr("E", "N"), f_UN = fr("U", "N"), f_NE = fr("N", "E"), f_NU = fr("N", "U"), f_EU = fr("E", "U"), f_UE = fr("U", "E"))]
no_flows <- FW[is.na(tot), date]   # months the CPS cannot link (fully) to the month before

# U-1 to U-10 under six assumptions. From U-3 up, every measure is (x + n) / (1 + n), with x what it counts inside the
# labor force and n what it counts outside it, both per labor-force member. U-1 and U-2 count particular kinds of
# unemployed people (the long-term unemployed, job losers), so people added to the labor force enter only their denominators.
fx <- function(x, n, k = "U3") if (k %in% c("U1", "U2")) round(100 * x / (1 + n), 6) else round(100 * (x + n) / (1 + n), 6)
d4 <- (L$U4 - L$U3) / (100 - L$U4)           # discouraged per labor-force member, from the official U-4
cm <- comp$main; u3 <- L$U3 / 100
X <- list(U1 = L$U1 / 100, U2 = L$U2 / 100, U3 = u3, U4 = u3, U5 = u3, U6 = u3 + L$p, U7 = u3 + L$p, U8 = u3 + L$p + cm$se,
          U9 = u3 + L$p + cm$se + cm$sei, U10 = u3 + L$p + cm$se + cm$sei + cm$sm)
N <- list(U1 = 0, U2 = 0, U3 = 0, U4 = d4, U5 = L$m, U6 = L$m, U7 = L$wj, U8 = L$wj, U9 = L$wj, U10 = L$wj)
e19 <- MW$m19 / lf_sa; e00 <- MW$m00 / lf_sa
# prime-age versions; the discouraged and the marginally attached are shared out by age in proportion to the want-a-job pool
# (job-market reasons, for the discouraged), because the microdata do not identify them. The prime-age file counts the
# mismatched (not part time for economic reasons) and the self-employed who are not mismatched; the mismatched self-employed
# are moved to the self-employment rungs in the national proportions, so prime-age U-10 is exact and U-8 and U-9 close.
f <- function(num, den) sa(num / den); fb <- function(num, den) sa(brk(num / den))
smu_p <- P0$smP * V$main$sm_seu / V$main$sm_np; smi_p <- P0$smP * V$main$sm_sei / V$main$sm_np
xp <- list(u15 = f(P0$u15, P0$lf), ulos = f(P0$ulos, P0$lf), u = f(P0$une, P0$lf), pt = f(P0$pter, P0$lf), sm = fb(P0$smP - smu_p - smi_p, P0$lf),
           se = fb(P0$seu + smu_p, P0$lf), sei = fb(P0$sei + smi_p, P0$lf), wj = f(P0$wj, P0$lf), nilf = f(P0$nilf, P0$lf))
dp <- d4 * f(D$lf * P0$wjmk / D$wjmk, P0$lf); mp <- L$m * f(D$lf * P0$wj / D$wj, P0$lf)
XP <- list(U1 = xp$u15, U2 = xp$ulos, U3 = xp$u, U4 = xp$u, U5 = xp$u, U6 = xp$u + xp$pt, U7 = xp$u + xp$pt, U8 = xp$u + xp$pt + xp$se,
           U9 = xp$u + xp$pt + xp$se + xp$sei, U10 = xp$u + xp$pt + xp$se + xp$sei + xp$sm)
NP <- list(U1 = 0, U2 = 0, U3 = 0, U4 = dp, U5 = mp, U6 = mp, U7 = xp$wj, U8 = xp$wj, U9 = xp$wj, U10 = xp$wj)
MS <- paste0("U", 1:10)
SCEN <- list(
  measured = setNames(lapply(MS, function(k) fx(X[[k]], N[[k]], k)), MS),
  want     = setNames(lapply(MS, function(k) fx(X[[k]], pmax(N[[k]], L$wj), k)), MS),   # the want-a-job pool contains the discouraged and the marginally attached
  p2019    = setNames(lapply(MS, function(k) fx(X[[k]], N[[k]] + e19, k)), MS),
  p2000    = setNames(lapply(MS, function(k) fx(X[[k]], N[[k]] + e00, k)), MS),
  prime    = setNames(lapply(MS, function(k) fx(XP[[k]], NP[[k]], k)), MS),
  everyone = setNames(lapply(MS, function(k) fx(XP[[k]], xp$nilf, k)), MS))       # every prime-age adult: U-3 becomes 100 minus the employment rate
stopifnot(max(abs(SCEN$measured$U6 - L$U6)) < 1e-3, max(abs(SCEN$measured$U7 - L$U7)) < 1e-3, max(abs(SCEN$measured$U10 - L$U10)) < 1e-3)
for (sc in names(SCEN)) for (k in MS) LFP[, (paste0(sc, "_", k)) := SCEN[[sc]][[k]]]
yrs <- function(v, y) mean(LFP[substr(date, 1, 4) == y, get(v)])
lastm <- max(L$date); li <- nrow(LFP)
since21 <- LFP[date >= "2021-01"]
LFPS <- list(
  last = lastm, no_flows = no_flows,
  latest = as.list(LFP[li, lapply(.SD, round, 2), .SDcols = c("lfpr", "epop", "lfpr_m", "lfpr_w", "epop_m", "epop_w", "lfpr_fb", "lfpr_nb", "nw_want", "nw_disab", "nw_retired", "nw_other", "f_EN", "f_UN", "f_NE", "f_EU")]),
  last3 = as.list(LFP[(li - 2):li, lapply(.SD, function(x) round(mean(x), 2)), .SDcols = c("f_EN", "f_UN", "f_NE", "f_EU", "f_UE", "f_NU")]),
  year12 = as.list(LFP[li - 12, lapply(.SD, round, 2), .SDcols = c("lfpr", "epop", "lfpr_m", "lfpr_w")]),
  bench = lapply(c(y2000 = "2000", y2007 = "2007", y2019 = "2019", y2023 = "2023", y2024 = "2024", y2025 = "2025"), function(y)
    sapply(c("lfpr", "epop", "lfpr_m", "lfpr_w", "epop_m", "epop_w", "lfpr_fb", "lfpr_nb", "nw_want", "nw_disab", "nw_retired", "nw_other", "f_EN", "f_UN", "f_NE", "f_EU"), function(v) round(yrs(v, y), 2), simplify = FALSE)),
  peak_since21 = list(lfpr = round(max(since21$lfpr), 2), date = since21[which.max(lfpr), date], epop = round(max(since21$epop), 2), epop_date = since21[which.max(epop), date]),
  low_2026 = list(lfpr = round(min(LFP[date >= "2026-01", lfpr]), 2), date = LFP[date >= "2026-01"][which.min(lfpr), date]),
  record = list(lfpr = round(max(LFP$lfpr), 2), date = LFP[which.max(lfpr), date]),
  missing = list(latest = as.list(round(MW[nrow(MW), .(m00, m07, m19, m00_men, m00_women, m19_men, m19_women)] / 1e6, 2)),
                 peak19 = list(m = round(max(MW$m19) / 1e6, 2), date = MW[which.max(m19), date]), peak00 = list(m = round(max(MW$m00) / 1e6, 2), date = MW[which.max(m00), date]),
                 share_lf = list(e19 = round(100 * tail(e19, 1), 2), e00 = round(100 * tail(e00, 1), 2))),
  scen_latest = lapply(SCEN, function(z) sapply(z, function(v) round(tail(v, 1), 1), simplify = FALSE)),
  scen_2019 = lapply(SCEN, function(z) sapply(z, function(v) round(mean(v[substr(L$date, 1, 4) == "2019"]), 1), simplify = FALSE)),
  scen_2010 = lapply(SCEN, function(z) sapply(z, function(v) round(v[L$date == "2009-10"], 1), simplify = FALSE)))
str(LFPS[c("latest", "peak_since21", "low_2026", "record")])
str(LFPS$missing)
rbindlist(lapply(names(SCEN), function(sc) data.table(scenario = sc, t(round(sapply(SCEN[[sc]], function(v) tail(v, 1)), 1)))))
```

```{r export}
r2 <- function(x, d = 3) round(x, d)
out <- cbind(L[, c("date", SER), with = FALSE], GSER[, !"date"])
fwrite(out, "data/u7_series.csv")
lastm <- max(L$date)
summary <- list(
  updated = format(Sys.Date()), last = lastm, missing = D[is.na(lf), date], params = params[c("alpha", "k", "w", "theta", "window")],
  latest = as.list(L[date == lastm, lapply(.SD, r2, 1), .SDcols = c(LADDER, "c_u", "c_ma", "c_pt", "c_wj", "c_seu", "c_sei", "c_sm")]),
  mean = as.list(L[, lapply(.SD, function(x) r2(mean(x), 1)), .SDcols = LADDER]),
  range = lapply(setNames(LADDER, LADDER), function(nm) r2(range(L[[nm]]), 1)),
  peak2020 = as.list(L[date == "2020-04", lapply(.SD, r2, 1), .SDcols = LADDER]),
  occupations = nrow(POOLED), req_levels = as.list(table(POOLED$p75)),
  sm_latest_lf = r2(100 * tail(comp$main$sm, 1), 2), sm_latest_emp = r2(100 * GC[date == lastm, sum(smP_all) / sum(emp)], 1),
  break2003 = as.list(r2(100 * sapply(comp, function(z) z$break_sm), 2)),
  validation = lapply(validation, r2), wj_mean = r2(100 * mean(L$wj), 2), ma_mean = r2(100 * mean(L$m), 2),
  tp = TP[, .(measure, scale, alpha = r2(alpha, 2), rec, status, onset, lead, head_start, dur, after_trough, n_sig, n_true, false)],
  cycle = list(cor_wj_u6 = r2(cyc$cor_wj_u6, 2), cor_se_u6 = r2(cyc$cor_se_u6, 2), cor_sm_u6 = r2(cyc$cor_sm_u6, 2), sd12 = as.list(r2(cyc$sd12, 2)),
               recessions = cyc$recessions[, lapply(.SD, function(x) if (is.numeric(x)) r2(x, 2) else x)]),
  self_employed = cls_mix[, .(class, share_emp = r2(share_emp, 1), ba = r2(ba, 1), mgmt = r2(mgmt, 1))],
  recovery = recov[, .(id, measure, low = r2(low, 2), high = r2(high, 2), left24 = r2(left24, 2), left48 = r2(left48, 2))],
  groups_tp = gtp[, .(group, measure, lead = r2(lead, 2), caught, n_sig, n_true, precision)],
  mismatch = list(by_group = mis[, .(group, rate = r2(rate, 1), n = round(n))], ba = mis_ba[, .(group, rate = r2(rate, 1), n = round(n))],
                  recent_grads = mis_grad[, .(group, rate = r2(rate, 1), n = round(n))], window = range(last24),
                  ba_by_year = mis_ba_year[order(race, year), .(year, race, rate = r2(rate, 1))]),
  sensitivity = sens[, lapply(.SD, function(x) if (is.numeric(x)) r2(x, 2) else x)],
  classic = classic,
  top_occupations = top_occ[, .(occ2010, label, required, counted_from, emp_k = round(emp / 1e3), mism_k = round(mism / 1e3), share = r2(share, 1))],
  validation_series = list(dates = V3$date, u3_micro = r2(V3$micro, 2), pter_micro = r2(VP$micro, 2), pter_official = r2(VP$official, 2)))
writeLines(toJSON(summary, auto_unbox = TRUE, na = "null", digits = NA, pretty = FALSE), "data/u7_summary.json")
fwrite(LFP, "data/u7_lfp.csv")
writeLines(toJSON(LFPS, auto_unbox = TRUE, na = "null", digits = NA, pretty = FALSE), "data/u7_lfp.json")
cat("Wrote data/u7_series.csv, data/u7_summary.json, data/u7_lfp.csv and data/u7_lfp.json\n")
```
